# 2.6.0

- Add `Observe.exposeStoreLazyLine` / `Observe.syncStoreLazyLine`: a resumable progressive merge
  fill for links slow enough that a monolithic keyframe cannot cross them. For lines whose
  top-level value is absolute and last-write-wins, per-key convergence replaces point-in-time
  consistency, which removes the frozen snapshot, the second copy in memory and the
  restart-on-change that a strict chunked transfer needs.
- There is no snapshot — not of values, and not of a key list either. Progress is one cursor the
  SUBSCRIBER holds, `{key, revision}` meaning "I have every key up to `key`, as of `revision`".
  The host keeps no per-subscriber state, so a reconnect resumes the fill instead of restarting
  it, which matters most on exactly the links this line exists for.
- Values are read AT SEND TIME. A key rewritten beyond the cursor is never sent twice and still
  lands its newest value; a key changed behind the cursor is re-sent. Those two rules are the
  whole convergence argument — there is no reconciliation pass. A deleted key behind the cursor
  travels as a tombstone; `tombstoneKeepMs` (default 10 min) bounds how long that stays provable,
  and a cursor older than the last prune is refused with `stale` rather than silently served,
  because continuing would leave deleted keys alive in the mirror forever.
- Delivery is pull-based: `readBytes` bounds every call, so a background fill cannot occupy a slow
  link ahead of an urgent line — the same head-of-line problem that starves the heartbeat in
  `experiments/slow-network-2026-08`. The budget must stay above the link's bandwidth-delay
  product or the link idles between reads; the rule is documented on the option.
- Cover suppression beyond the cursor, re-send behind it, tombstone behaviour on both sides of
  the cursor, resume after a dropped connection, catch-up of what changed while away, refusal of a
  cursor older than tombstone retention, read-budget bounding, and convergence of a 350-key mirror
  under continuous churn.
- Add `experiments/store-lazy-2026-08`: both candidates over a real socket.io + RPC connection
  through the shared metered relay, same Store, same churn. Extract that relay to
  `experiments/_shared/metered-relay.ts` so a second stand cannot drift into a private copy.
- The stand caught three implementation faults before release, all fixed. One patch object per key
  repeated `path`/`value`/`exists` per entry and cost 2.8x the bytes of the equivalent keyframe;
  chunks now carry a compact key/value map. A read budget below the bandwidth-delay product made
  the fill latency-bound; convergence over 20 000 keys improved from 112.6 s to 18.8 s. The
  session handshake delayed first paint; the stateless cursor removed it.
- Measured boundary at ~1 Mbit/s: on 20 000 keys the lazy line reaches first paint in 718 ms
  against 11 579 ms for a keyframe — 16x — while sending 6 % fewer bytes, paid for with 1.33x
  slower full convergence. On a 350-key Store it is at parity when quiet and ~1.6x slower under
  churn, with no first-paint advantage. Use this surface when first paint on a large Store is the
  dominant requirement.
